description: Make the input fields fit inside the card. .control is width: 100% with padding and a border, and nothing sets box-sizing: border-box, so the browser adds the padding on top of the full width and every field overflows the card by about 26 pixels either side. This is the one fault on the page that is visible without reading the tests.

Every failed sign-in returns the same message, whatever was wrong with it. auth.authenticate currently says 'We do not have an account with that username' for an unknown username and 'That password is not correct' for a bad password, which tells an anonymous visitor which usernames exist. Use auth.FAILURE for every failure. A failure must still carry a message; identical is not the same as absent.

Give both inputs a real <label for=...> with words in it, keeping their ids, and mark the error paragraph so a screen reader announces it (role='alert' or aria-live). The controls are currently named by placeholder alone, which vanishes on typing and is not announced reliably. The error region must exist in the document before there is an error to put in it.

Make the failure message readable. The --danger custom property in static/style.css is #f4f6f8 against a #ffffff card, a contrast ratio of 1.08:1 where WCAG asks 4.5:1 for body text, so the message is present in the HTML and invisible on screen. Choose a colour that reaches 4.5:1 against the card and is distinct from ordinary body text.
